'''Élisabeth Bouscaren''' (born 1956)<ref>Birth year from [https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb13592294h BNF catalog entry], accessed 2018-10-08</ref> is a French mathematician who works on algebraic geometry, algebra and mathematical logic (model theory).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.u-psud.fr/~bouscare/|title=Elisabeth Bouscaren|website=www.math.u-psud.fr|access-date=2018-10-08}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Bouscaren received her doctorate in 1979 from the [[University of Paris VII]] and her habilitation in 1985. From 1981 she worked at the [[French National Center for Scientific Research]] (CNRS) until 2005, when she moved to the [[University of Paris XI]]. Since 2007, she has held the position of Research Director at CNRS.

She has been a visiting scholar at [[Yale University]], the [[University of Notre Dame]] and [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]], and has published a book on [[Ehud Hrushovski]]'s proof of the [[Glossary of arithmetic and diophantine geometry|Mordell-Lang]] conjecture.
She was an invited speaker in the logic session of the 2002 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].<ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers], accessed 2018-10-08</ref>

In 2020, Bouscaren gave the [[Gödel Lecture]], titled ''The ubiquity of configurations in Model Theory.''
